However, it is more challenging to execute a backstab with a heavy weapon. Currently, in this game, backstabs seem balanced: the more damage your weapon inflicts during a backstab, the longer the confirmation animation lasts.

The issue arises with instant backstabs, as seen in earlier versions of the game, combined with a non-ideal connection, making it a strategy that doesn't require much skill to execute.

Backstabs should serve as a strategic option to regain stamina and reposition when your opponent recovers, rather than being an offensive move on their own.

The combat in this game is deep. Yes, it is significantly slower than its sequel and even slower than its predecessor. The movement also feels more floaty and the weapon impacts lack real weight. However, the level of control over your actions is still present.

There are a lot of weapons, some of which have the same moves but different appearances, ranges, and stats. That said, there is still a lot of weapon variety, and you have plenty of options depending on your character build.

The power stance is also a cool feature, allowing you to use different weapon combinations for dual attacks with specific buttons (though you'll need high stats for this).

That said, the game is fantastic. It has tons of content, a lot of variety in levels and bosses (though the level design is a step back from the other games), and many weapons, with viable magic, sorceries, pyromancies, and faith (though faith is mostly for buffs in this game).

There are many bosses (31 in the base game, 40 with the expansions), but most of the base game ones are forgettable (though many have interesting concepts).

The expansions and their bosses are designed for end-game, significantly harder than the base game, and are among the best content in all games of this genre, featuring amazing boss fights.

Overall, if you can overlook the inferior level and world design, less memorable base game bosses, and a different, slightly slower gameplay, then you'll enjoy it a lot; it has tons of replayability (and great player-versus-player as well).
